Description

Typed selection over detached tmux observations.

Build a Query with a source and matching, then use runQuery to read an existing Snapshot without IO. fetch explicitly acquires a new snapshot. Ordinary lists and application predicates remain available through LibTmux.Snapshot; portable expressions contain no callbacks.

Import field modules qualified: LibTmux.Query.Pane, LibTmux.Query.Session, LibTmux.Query.Window, LibTmux.Query.Link, LibTmux.Query.Occurrence, LibTmux.Query.Client, LibTmux.Query.ClientAttachment and LibTmux.Query.ServerInfo. Field tokens describe captured values; reading them never contacts tmux.

Query construction, operands and results are finite. Execution validates every declared requirement before filtering, stably ordering and limiting. The default source order and multiplicity come from the supplied snapshot. A result establishes what was observed, not current liveness or a reserved command target. See exactlyOne before selecting an explicit reference.

>>> exactlyOne [1 :: Integer]
Right 1
>>> exactlyOne ([] :: [Integer])
Left NoMatches
>>> atMostOne ([] :: [Integer])
Right Nothing
>>> atMostOne [1, 2 :: Integer]
Left AtLeastTwoMatches

Descriptions

data Field row value Source #

Fields belong to physical rows or contextual links, never both implicitly.

data Expr row Source #

A pure predicate description for one row type. Field and relationship tokens retain their identity; arbitrary application functions stay outside this portable representation. Nominal roles prevent cross-row coercion.

data Query row Source #

A source, predicate, stable ordering and optional final limit. Building a query performs no IO and retains no Server handle. Use LibTmux.Query to evaluate.

data Order row Source #

One ascending or descending field ordering. Combine keys with orderBy.

data ToMany parent child Source #

A closed one-to-many relationship. Obtain tokens from the entity field modules and use some, every or none. Constructors are private.

data ToOne parent child Source #

A required relationship in a validated graph, used with related.

data ToOptional parent child Source #

An observed optional relationship, used with optionalRelated. Known absence is separate from an unavailable relationship.

Scalar predicates

eq :: Eq value => Field row value -> value -> Expr row Source #

Exact equality in the field's declared type. No Unicode normalization, case folding or byte-to-text conversion is implicit.

oneOf :: Eq value => Field row value -> [value] -> Expr row Source #

Membership using exact equality against a finite operand list. An empty list never matches, but its field requirement is still validated.

contains :: Field row Text -> Text -> Expr row Source #

Exact, case-sensitive Text substring matching. Byte-bearing fields are deliberately excluded; use typed equality for their retained values.

ge :: Field row Integer -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Compare a mathematical Integer field with an unbounded threshold: greater-or-equal, greater, less-or-equal or less, respectively.

gt :: Field row Integer -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Compare a mathematical Integer field with an unbounded threshold: greater-or-equal, greater, less-or-equal or less, respectively.

le :: Field row Integer -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Compare a mathematical Integer field with an unbounded threshold: greater-or-equal, greater, less-or-equal or less, respectively.

lt :: Field row Integer -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Compare a mathematical Integer field with an unbounded threshold: greater-or-equal, greater, less-or-equal or less, respectively.

dimensionAtLeast :: Field row Dimension -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Compare a positive cell dimension to an Integer threshold, inclusively. Negative and arbitrarily large thresholds are valid predicates; they do not construct a command dimension. Use not_ for a strict opposite bound.

dimensionAtMost :: Field row Dimension -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Compare a positive cell dimension to an Integer threshold, inclusively. Negative and arbitrarily large thresholds are valid predicates; they do not construct a command dimension. Use not_ for a strict opposite bound.

paneIndexAtLeast :: Field row PaneIndex -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Inclusive bounds on a pane index, without narrowing or constructing an index.

paneIndexAtMost :: Field row PaneIndex -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Inclusive bounds on a pane index, without narrowing or constructing an index.

windowIndexAtLeast :: Field row WindowIndex -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Inclusive bounds on a contextual window index, using Integer thresholds.

windowIndexAtMost :: Field row WindowIndex -> Integer -> Expr row Source #

Inclusive bounds on a contextual window index, using Integer thresholds.

Logic and relationships

allOf :: [Expr row] -> Expr row Source #

Finite conjunction and disjunction. Empty lists mean True and False, respectively. Validation checks every branch before evaluation short-circuits.

anyOf :: [Expr row] -> Expr row Source #

Finite conjunction and disjunction. Empty lists mean True and False, respectively. Validation checks every branch before evaluation short-circuits.

not_ :: Expr row -> Expr row Source #

Logical negation, preserving the expression's validation requirements.

some :: ToMany row child -> Expr child -> Expr row Source #

Existential, universal or absent matching children. A known empty relationship yields False, True or True, respectively. The child expression applies to one child at a time; put conditions inside one allOf when the same child must satisfy them. Unavailable relationships remain errors.

every :: ToMany row child -> Expr child -> Expr row Source #

Existential, universal or absent matching children. A known empty relationship yields False, True or True, respectively. The child expression applies to one child at a time; put conditions inside one allOf when the same child must satisfy them. Unavailable relationships remain errors.

none :: ToMany row child -> Expr child -> Expr row Source #

Existential, universal or absent matching children. A known empty relationship yields False, True or True, respectively. The child expression applies to one child at a time; put conditions inside one allOf when the same child must satisfy them. Unavailable relationships remain errors.

related :: ToOne row child -> Expr child -> Expr row Source #

Test the required related observation in the supplied snapshot. A failed lookup returns RelationshipLookupFailed, never False or absence.

optionalRelated :: ToOptional row child -> Expr child -> Expr row Source #

Test a known optional target. Absence yields False, so negation includes absence as well as targets that fail the child predicate.

Selection and ordering

matching :: Expr row -> Query row -> Query row Source #

Conjoin a predicate with existing predicates without changing the source.

orderBy :: [Order row] -> Query row -> Query row Source #

Replace the ordering keys. Sorting is stable and follows filtering; an empty key list retains source order. Limits are always applied afterward.

ascending :: Ord value => Field row value -> Order row Source #

Order by the declared field's Ord instance in ascending or descending order. Text and byte-bearing types retain their own comparison semantics.

descending :: Ord value => Field row value -> Order row Source #

Order by the declared field's Ord instance in ascending or descending order. Text and byte-bearing types retain their own comparison semantics.

limit :: Natural -> Query row -> Query row Source #

Replace the final nonnegative limit, applied after filtering and ordering regardless of builder order. A zero limit still validates every requirement.

runQuery :: Snapshot -> Query row -> Either QueryError [row] Source #

Validate and evaluate against the supplied complete snapshot. Every requirement is checked before reading rows, including empty sources and zero limits. Consuming a successful result performs only pure processing of owned observations. No acquisition, pushdown or refresh occurs.

fetch :: Server -> Query row -> IO (Either QueryError [row]) Source #

Acquire a complete fresh snapshot and evaluate the query against it. Compiled evaluator support is checked before IO; version requirements are checked against acquired server metadata. Operational failures propagate as exceptions from capture; use tryTmux to retain their context and recovery owners. Cancellation propagates unchanged.

This performs one acquisition per call, even when the query is reused or has a zero limit. Use runQuery to reuse an existing Snapshot. No filter is pushed into tmux in this implementation.

Cardinality

data CardinalityError Source #

Selection cardinality without retaining observations or counting ambiguity.

Constructors

NoMatches

The selection is empty where one value was required.

AtLeastTwoMatches

A second match exists; no complete count is computed.

exactlyOne :: [row] -> Either CardinalityError row Source #

Require exactly one value. Uniqueness can require traversing the entire input; ambiguity is established at the second match without forcing its tail. This neither acquires data nor reserves a live command target.

atMostOne :: [row] -> Either CardinalityError (Maybe row) Source #

Permit absence but reject a second match, with the same traversal behavior as exactlyOne. Use ordinary listToMaybe when choosing the first is intended.
